proposals.before: Xie Ju, whose courtesy name was Yanyang, was the younger brother of Xie Lan, Director of the Palace Library.
proposals.after: Xie Ju, whose courtesy name was Yanyang, was the younger brother of Xie Lan, Director of the Palace Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 中書令 is the Palace Secretariat director, not the Palace Library (秘書監).

proposals.before: Earlier the northern scholar Lu Guang, skilled in Confucian learning, was Libationer of the National University; when he lectured there, Vice Director Xu Mian and the rest all attended.
proposals.after: Earlier the northern scholar Lu Guang, skilled in Confucian learning, was Erudite of the National University; when he lectured there, Vice Director Xu Mian and the rest all attended.
proposals.reason: 國子博士 is Erudite/Doctor of the National University, not Libationer (祭酒).

proposals.before: In the sixth year he returned as Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Library; before he could assume the latter post he was made Grand Warden of the Heir Apparent and General of the Left Guards, still Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: In the sixth year he returned as Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat; before he could assume the latter post he was made Grand Warden of the Heir Apparent and General of the Left Guards, still Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: 中書監 is Director of the Palace Secretariat, not Palace Library (秘書監).

proposals.before: Ju’s father Xie Yue in Qi times had died in this very office, and Ju repeatedly submitted memorials begging to resign and receive another appointment, but the edict did not permit it; only after a long time did he finally take up the post.
proposals.after: Ju’s father Xie Yue in Qi times had ended his career in this very office, and Ju repeatedly submitted memorials begging to resign and receive another appointment, but the edict did not permit it; only after a long time did he finally take up the post.
proposals.reason: 終此官 means ended his career in the office; the literal invents death.

proposals.before: Censor Zhang Zan charged that Jingrong had used private ties to mislead the throne and deserved death; an edict spared his life but stripped him of office.
proposals.after: Censor Zhang Wan charged that Jingrong had used private ties to mislead the throne and deserved death; an edict spared his life but stripped him of office.
proposals.reason: 張綰 is Zhang Wan; Zan does not match 綰.

proposals.before: In Song, Wang Hongjing sat at the head yet never opened a file; elegance was admired, and the current ran deep.
proposals.after: In Song, Wang Jinghong sat at the head yet never opened a file; elegance was admired, and the current ran deep.
proposals.reason: 王敬弘 is Jinghong; the translation reverses the name characters.

decisions.reason: s0003 has 中書令覽; 中書令 is Director of the Palace Secretariat, not the Palace Library (秘書監).
s0017 has 爲國子博士; 國子博士 is Erudite of the National University, not Libationer (祭酒).
s0026 has 侍中、中書監; 中書監 is Director of the Palace Secretariat, not Palace Library (秘書監).
齊世終此官 means he ended his career in that office under Qi; the literal’s “died” invents death not present in 終此官.
s0060 names 御史中丞張綰; 綰 is Wan, so Zhang Zan is a false reading.
s0094 has 王敬弘; given name 敬弘 is Jinghong, not the reversed Hongjing.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0003 shows English Palace Library came only from misreading 中書監; the office claim must read Palace Secretariat while keeping zh, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0005 shows English Zan came only from misreading 綰; the personal-name claim must read Zhang Wan while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0006 shows English Hongjing came only from reversing 敬弘; the personal-name claim must read Wang Jinghong while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
